Three resolution changes that cut the manual `--include` flags real-world  
npm projects need for `deno compile --bundle`, plus an opt-in `--minify`  
flag. Same parity ballpark as `bun build --compile`.

**Reverse-walk for native-addon packages.** The NAPI-RS layout splits a  
JS-only wrapper package from one binary package per platform. Only the  
binary one has a `.node` file, so the existing forward closure missed the  
wrapper, which is the package user code actually imports. The platform  
binary shipped but the wrapper didn't, so the runtime `require` returned  
null and the addon silently failed to load. A one-level reverse walk (any  
package whose deps include a native-addon package) recovers the wrapper.

**Broaden worker URL discovery.** The previous version only matched the  
inline form `new Worker(new URL("X", import.meta.url), ...)`. Real code  
often stashes the URL in a variable first  
(`const workerUrl = new URL(...); new Worker(workerUrl)`) and uses a ternary  
to pick between `.ts`/`.js` variants, so the old regex saw nothing. Now  
every `new URL(<arg>, import.meta.url)` call is scanned, each string literal  
inside `<arg>` is walked (handling the ternary), and the basename is  
searched across the workspace. Anything that resolves to a `.ts`/`.js`/etc  
file becomes a worker entry: bundled separately, embedded next to the main  
bundle, URL string rewritten in place.

**Auto-include the closest `package.json`.** Packages that read their own  
`package.json` at runtime for version info walk up from `import.meta.url`;  
after bundling the bundle sits next to none, so the walk falls back to  
`__dirname` and the read errors. Auto-including the closest `package.json`  
to the entrypoint means the walk succeeds out of the box.

**`--minify` flag.** Adds an experimental `deno compile --minify` (only  
meaningful with `--bundle`) that minifies the embedded bundle, reducing both  
the embedded payload size and runtime memory use, at the cost of less  
readable stack traces. The dynamic-`require` shim rewrite was generalized to  
match esbuild's minified variable names so `require` keeps working in  
minified output.

Together these let projects that previously needed a handful of manual  
`--include` flags build with none. All `compile::bundle::*` spec tests pass.

Stacks on [#34531](https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/34531)
. After PR 2/3 the binary was correct but wasteful: if
any CJS package or native addon survived bundling, we shipped the
entire resolved npm tree. For the lodash hello-world that was 11.6 MB
of payload; for \`@node-rs/crc32\` it was 10.6 MB.

Make use of the data the path-rewriter already has. Every absolute
path it rewrote in the bundle (and in each worker bundle) is the
runtime require target of a CJS module; the binary writer maps each
back to its owning npm package by longest-prefix folder match, walks
the dep closure, and embeds only those \`<.deno>/<id>/node\_modules/\`
directories. That parent dir is important — embedding just the
canonical package folder loses the sibling symlinks the deno linker
creates for direct deps (NAPI-RS-style optional platform packages),
so requires that walk into a sibling fail.

Real reductions on the same fixtures used to validate PRs 2-3:

- lodash hello-world: 11.62 MB → 1.45 MB payload (~8x)
- \`@node-rs/crc32\` hello-world: 10.62 MB → 468 KB payload (~23x)
- chalk hello-world (pure ESM): unchanged at 17 KB

The full snapshot still ships in metadata so node-module resolution by
name works at runtime; only the on-disk file content shrinks. BYONM
keeps the old whole-tree behavior for now (precise scoping needs
workspace-layout awareness).

``[feat(compile): cover CJS-deep imports under --bundle](https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/34536/commits/2bbe0e4ee91d7c585e5d6212dd957eccaf7ae665 "feat(compile): cover CJS-deep imports under --bundle  Stacks on #34532. Three small fixes to make `compile --bundle` work for real npm trees instead of just toy fixtures.  When the bundle phase of `compile --bundle` ran, the module-graph creation underneath inherited the `Compile` subcommand's factory configuration. That meant deep CJS files inside `node_modules` (e.g. `jiti/dist/jiti.cjs` imported via `import _ from "../dist/jiti.cjs"` in `jiti/lib/jiti.mjs`) never made it into the graph, and esbuild's load handler returned nothing for them. The parent .mjs then tripped a parse error before bundling could finish. The minimum a real project needs is the same factory settings that `deno bundle` uses for those three knobs: `bundle_mode` in the node-resolver config, `node_code_translator_mode` set to `Disabled`, and `allow_json_imports` set to `Always`. Adding a single `internal.force_bundle_mode` flag and threading it into those three sites — set by `bundle_for_compile` only for the duration of bundling — is enough; the surrounding compile flow keeps Compile-subcommand semantics for everything else.  With the translator-mode change, CJS native-addon packages stopped resolving: `require('./build/Release/foo')` (no extension) used to auto-resolve to `foo.node` through the CJS analyzer's path, which doesn't run in Disabled mode, and esbuild's resolver only tried `.js` as a fallback. Two follow-up tweaks: extend the resolver's NotFound-on-Require fallback to also try `.node` (matching Node's documented `require` resolution order), and short-circuit any resolved path ending in `.node` to `external: true` in the bundle's `on_resolve` so esbuild doesn't try to load it as JS. needs is the same factory settings that \`deno bundle\` uses for those
three knobs: \`bundle\_mode\` in the node-resolver config,
\`node\_code\_translator\_mode\` set to \`Disabled\`, and \`allow\_json\_imports\`
set to \`Always\`. Adding a single \`internal.force\_bundle\_mode\` flag and
threading it into those three sites — set by \`bundle\_for\_compile\` only
for the duration of bundling — is enough; the surrounding compile
flow keeps Compile-subcommand semantics for everything else.

With the translator-mode change, CJS native-addon packages stopped
resolving: \`require('./build/Release/foo')\` (no extension) used to
auto-resolve to \`foo.node\` through the CJS analyzer's path, which
doesn't run in Disabled mode, and esbuild's resolver only tried \`.js\`
as a fallback. Two follow-up tweaks: extend the resolver's
NotFound-on-Require fallback to also try \`.node\` (matching Node's
documented \`require\` resolution order), and short-circuit any resolved
path ending in \`.node\` to \`external: true\` in the bundle's \`on\_resolve\`
so esbuild doesn't try to load it as JS.

All four \`compile::bundle::\*\` spec tests still pass, and a real
end-to-end build of \`earendil-works/pi\` (~2700 modules, jiti included)
now goes from "parse error" to a running binary.
